items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented 2025-03-14 (Condition I480) during the admission for embolic cerebral infarction; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered (chart shows only metoprolol, famotidine, levothyroxine; cardiology notes through 2026-06-23 list no anticoagulant). CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (female 1, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior ischemic stroke 2), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. Needs review for starting a DOAC.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start - requirement met. (That ECG showed QTc ~563 ms, handled as a separate QT_SAFETY item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. Because the medication was started before 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies, so an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc ~435 ms) - requirement met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. As the start was on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc ~375 ms) - requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days (by 4/24/2026). The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start and outside the required window - so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of the 9/24/2026 review. (The late ECG showed sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc ~377 ms.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (not on the medication list at the 2/18/2026 visit; the only earlier exposure was a brief inpatient course ending 1/1/2026). An ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/15/2026). No ECG has been obtained since 12/25/2025, so the monitoring ECG is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days (by 8/24/2026). No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but the requirement is not yet due at the 9/24/2026 review date; it should be scheduled before 9/29/2026.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 (subtherapeutic) and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days (by 9/8/2026). INR(PT) 2.3 was drawn 9/5/2026 (Observation 4282f19b), within the window - requirement met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a warfarin dose change made under the clinic protocol (home INR 3.4; warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily). The 3/1/2026 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 6/17/2026 (INR 2.7), so the confirmatory INR is overdue as of 9/24/2026 in a 95-year-old also taking amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 (Condition 42731) and carried in the problem list of every subsequent cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025, 11/20/2025, 3/13/2026, 6/27/2026). No anticoagulant is or has been ordered; current medications are levothyroxine only (amiodarone was a brief peri-operative course ending 8/27/2025). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis = vascular disease 1), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (2025-08-22) should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulant needs prescriber review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order valid to 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, even though outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 document an upper GI bleed from a duodenal ulcer (admission 8/2-8/5/2026, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Also on aspirin and clopidogrel. The decision to resume anticoagulation after a major bleed has not been documented and needs prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are current simultaneously. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs in the current medication list. Rivaroxaban was never stopped, so as of 9/24/2026 the patient has concurrent rivaroxaban and apixaban (plus clopidogrel) - a bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 142-144 bpm with no organised P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD ~100 ms, no reproducible atrial deflection) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, and unspecified atrial fibrillation was coded for the same encounter. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the tracings; the note needs correction and rate/rhythm management reviewed.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current clinic order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026; continuously prescribed since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~500 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~535 ms, which is >=500 ms and per the QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L (3/18/2026) and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven; note the 5/14/2024 clinic note called the QT 'acceptable' when starting escitalopram. A repeat ECG and review of QT-prolonging therapy are needed.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current clinic order 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027; started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QT ~555 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~563 ms - markedly prolonged and >=500 ms, which requires prescriber review under the QT monitoring memo. QTc was 414 ms on the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025, so this is a drug-associated increase of ~150 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Also on warfarin; amiodarone dose/continuation and repeat ECG need review.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current clinic order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027; on citalopram since 3/8/2025). Most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~505 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~549 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, requiring prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. QTc was 424 ms on the previous ECG (6/17/2020). Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised with QT prolongation; dose reduction and a repeat ECG should be considered.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current clinic order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027; on amiodarone since at least 2022). Most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a broad, late-peaking T wave: QT ~575 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~565 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold that requires prescriber review. Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal. She is also on warfarin (dose just changed 9/10/2026) and metoprolol; amiodarone continuation and a current ECG need review.

interpretations.explanation: 3/7/2026 tracing (only ECG on file). Regular P waves preceding every QRS at 81 bpm with normal PR 184 ms; narrow QRS 68 ms, QT 322 ms giving Bazett QTc 375 ms; frontal axis +45 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Confirms sinus rhythm as documented in the same-day clinic note despite the coded history of atrial fibrillation; no prior tracing for comparison.

7/15/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm at 104 bpm with prominent P waves, PR 118 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT ~345 ms, QTc 454 ms, axis +40 degrees, no conduction block. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed a regular sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with P waves partly fused with the preceding T wave (QTc approximately 440 ms after separating the P wave); rhythm, conduction and QTc are therefore not materially changed.

5/21/2024 tracing (only ECG on file): sinus tachycardia 110 bpm, PR 116 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 338 ms, QTc 457 ms (mildly prolonged; no QT-watch-list drug in the chart), axis +36 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block.

6/10/2026 19:36 tracing: irregularly irregular rhythm at a mean ventricular rate of ~144 bpm with absent P waves (RR 0.35-0.65 s, RMSSD ~100 ms) - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, so no measurable PR. QRS 94 ms, QT ~287 ms, QTc 445 ms, axis 0 degrees, no bundle branch block. The tracing 2 hours earlier the same day (107914094) shows the same atrial fibrillation at 142 bpm with QTc 444 ms, so no change. This contradicts the clinic note of the same day that reports 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (see the CONTRADICTION item).

8/2/2025 tracing: regular sinus rhythm 69 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 403 ms, QTc 432 ms; frontal axis about -25 degrees (lead II nearly isoelectric) - within normal limits. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 had a grossly negative lead I with the precordial leads normal (suggesting arm-lead reversal, calculated axis -174 degrees) and QTc 405 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the QTc difference is 27 ms.
5/23/2024 tracing (only ECG on file): sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, PR 111 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, QT 302 ms, QTc 384 ms, axis +4 degrees. No conduction abnormality.

12/25/2025 tracing (only ECG on file): sinus rhythm 72 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 362 ms, QTc 397 ms, axis +22 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. This predates the escitalopram started 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the post-start monitoring ECG (see FOLLOW_UP item).

11/15/2024 tracing: irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no P waves (RR 0.69-1.17 s, RMSSD 308 ms), mean ventricular rate ~59 bpm - atrial fibrillation with a controlled/slow ventricular response, so no measurable PR. QRS 84 ms, QT 424 ms, QTc 420 ms, axis +30 degrees. The prior ECG three days earlier (11/12/2024) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves (PR 170 ms) and QTc 393 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

3/9/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, PR 107 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 421 ms, QTc 415 ms, axis +60 degrees, no block. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was essentially identical (62 bpm, QTc 436 ms); no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change. This tracing long predates the haloperidol started 9/15/2026 (see FOLLOW_UP item).
8/23/2025 tracing (only ECG on file): regular sinus rhythm 83 bpm, PR 144 ms, narrow QRS 64 ms, QT 314 ms, QTc 407 ms, axis +53 degrees. No conduction abnormality.

6/19/2020 tracing: sinus rhythm 77 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 414 ms, QTc 468 ms (borderline prolonged), axis +65 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2/2/2020: sinus rhythm 75 bpm with QTc ~511 ms; the QTc has fallen by about 43 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold, and rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

1/18/2021 tracing: sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT 274 ms with QTc 388 ms, axis +51 degrees, no conduction block. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QTc 392 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

6/23/2025 tracing: sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm; every QRS is preceded by a P wave but the PR interval is prolonged at about 216 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms (no bundle branch block), QT 398 ms, QTc 379 ms, frontal axis approximately +20 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 showed sinus bradycardia 50 bpm with PR at the upper limit of normal (~190 ms) and QTc 362 ms; no rhythm, bundle branch or QTc change of 60 ms.

9/13/2025 07:17 tracing: irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, mean ventricular rate ~150 bpm (RR 0.31-0.60 s), with no organised atrial activity - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, no measurable PR. QRS ~60-75 ms, QT 258 ms, QTc 408 ms, axis -9 degrees. The tracing the previous evening (9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at ~77 bpm with a single premature beat, PR 154 ms and QTc 411 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new. Corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded 9/11-9/13/2025; he is now on apixaban.

11/23/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with clear P waves, PR 170 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 351 ms, QTc 388 ms, axis +11 degrees, no conduction block - confirming the 'sinus rhythm' documented in the same-day clinic note. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 showed sinus rhythm 67 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT (QTc ~527 ms); the QTc has since fallen by about 139 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 applies.
2/15/2025 tracing (only ECG on file): regular sinus rhythm 74 bpm, PR 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 78 ms, QT 360 ms, QTc 422 ms, axis +55 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block.

6/26/2023 tracing: sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular, PR 164 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 283 ms, QTc 386 ms, axis +35 degrees, no conduction block. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was very similar (sinus tachycardia 114 bpm, PR 168 ms, QTc 385 ms) - no change. No tracing is available since the 2025 atrial flutter diagnosis or the August 2026 GI bleed.

3/14/2025 tracing (only ECG on file): sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with a consistent P wave before each QRS (PR 176 ms) and a single premature beat followed by a compensatory pause (RR 0.54 s then 1.39 s) - not atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was coded the same day. QRS 96 ms, QT 398 ms, QTc 405 ms; frontal axis about -31 degrees with positive I/aVL and negative II/III/aVF = left axis deviation. No bundle branch block.

4/29/2026 tracing (only ECG on file): regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm with consistent atrial activity preceding each QRS, PR 139 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 351 ms, QTc 377 ms. Lead I is entirely negative (QRS, P and T inverted) while the precordial leads are normal, giving a calculated frontal axis of about -172 degrees (extreme/indeterminate quadrant); this pattern is typical of left/right arm lead reversal and repeat acquisition with correct lead placement is advised. No bundle branch block.

11/10/2023 tracing: sinus rhythm 70 bpm, PR 158 ms, QRS 86 ms, axis +37 degrees, no bundle branch block, but the T wave is broad with QT about 505 ms and Bazett QTc ~549 ms - markedly prolonged. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 (sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, right axis, QTc 424 ms) was normal, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms. She takes citalopram 40 mg daily (see QT_SAFETY item).

3/8/2026 tracing (only ECG on file), obtained 24 days after escitalopram was started: sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 143 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 408 ms, QTc 435 ms (below the 500 ms review threshold), axis +56 degrees, no conduction abnormality.

1/13/2019 tracing: sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 388 ms, QTc 364 ms, axis -4 degrees, no bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with low-amplitude complexes and QRS duration ~118 ms (incomplete, not meeting the 120 ms criterion for a bundle branch block) and QTc 390 ms; no coded conduction or QTc change.

10/8/2023 tracing: sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 84 ms, axis +45 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late-peaking with QT about 500 ms, giving Bazett QTc ~535 ms - markedly prolonged. The previous ECG (11/23/2022) had QTc 355 ms, so the QTc has risen by roughly 180 ms. Relevant because he takes escitalopram (see QT_SAFETY item).

7/13/2022 tracing: regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 0.40-0.45 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible P wave before every QRS (PR ~138 ms) and no sawtooth flutter waves in II/III/V1 - sinus tachycardia. QRS 74 ms, QT 270 ms, QTc 414 ms, axis 0 degrees, no block. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at ~113 bpm without P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved on this tracing. QTc change -15 ms.
5/12/2025 tracing (only ECG on file): sinus rhythm 82 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 372 ms, QTc 436 ms, axis +34 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block.

7/16/2022 tracing: sinus rhythm 91 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 74 ms, QT 330 ms, QTc 406 ms, frontal axis about -15 degrees (normal), no conduction block. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm 87 bpm with PR 116 ms and QTc 391 ms; no rhythm, conduction or 60 ms QTc change.

7/17/2024 tracing: sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with a P wave before each QRS but a prolonged PR of about 210 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is wide at ~120 ms with a QS/rS complex in V1-V2 and a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL, V5-V6 - left bundle branch block. QT 436 ms, QTc 440 ms, frontal axis about -21 degrees. The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 showed the same pattern (sinus rhythm with a pause, PR ~205 ms, QRS 136 ms LBBB, QTc 446 ms), so the bundle branch block is not new and the QTc is unchanged.

3/19/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 135 ms, QRS 78 ms, QT 326 ms, QTc 424 ms, axis +45 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Nearly identical to the prior tracing of 3/18/2025 (102 bpm, PR 128 ms, QTc 422 ms) - no change.

9/22/2025 tracing (only ECG on file): regular sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, PR 163 ms, narrow QRS 62 ms, QT 352 ms, QTc 369 ms; frontal axis about -22 degrees (lead II nearly isoelectric) - within the normal range. No bundle branch block or AV block.

4/27/2022 tracing: organised regular rhythm at 58 bpm with a discrete P wave before each QRS; the PR interval measures about 205 ms, just beyond the upper limit, so first-degree AV block is reported. QRS 74 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +39 degrees. The T wave is very broad and late-peaking with QT ~575 ms and Bazett QTc ~565 ms - severe QT prolongation in a patient on amiodarone (see QT_SAFETY item). The prior ECG of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at ~129 bpm with no P waves and QTc 428 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms.

5/1/2022 tracing: sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, PR 136 ms, narrow QRS (~55 ms), QT 292 ms, QTc 390 ms, axis +54 degrees, no conduction block. The prior ECG of 7/27/2019 showed sinus rhythm 75 bpm with QTc 429 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the QTc difference (-39 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold.

4/19/2024 tracing (only ECG on file): sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with consistent P waves, PR 130 ms, narrow QRS 66 ms, QT 280 ms, QTc 397 ms, axis +69 degrees. No conduction abnormality. No prior tracing for comparison.

8/23/2021 10:07 tracing: sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 139 ms, QRS 82 ms, QT 318 ms, QTc 413 ms, axis +57 degrees, no block. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (101 bpm, QTc 409 ms); no change.

10/24/2024 tracing: sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with P waves before each QRS (PR 166 ms); QRS 86 ms, QT 425 ms, QTc 395 ms, axis +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 showed sinus rhythm ~57 bpm with an isolated premature beat and QTc 346 ms; QTc change +49 ms (below the 60 ms threshold) and no rhythm or conduction change. Note that sinus rhythm is present despite his coded atrial fibrillation (he remains on warfarin).

12/5/2024 14:38 tracing: regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 82 ms with an rSR' pattern in V1 and deep S waves in I/aVL/V6 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern, QRS below 120 ms so not coded), QT 292 ms with QTc 415 ms; lead I QRS is nearly isoelectric/negative with positive aVF and III, i.e. right axis deviation. The earlier tracing the same day (01:33) showed sinus rhythm 100 bpm with a wider (~115 ms) rSR' in V1 and QTc ~470 ms; neither meets criteria for complete bundle branch block and the QTc difference is under 60 ms, so no change is coded.

11/24/2025 tracing: sinus rhythm 62 bpm (one late premature beat), PR 168 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis +67 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT is grossly prolonged at about 555 ms with Bazett QTc ~563 ms. The previous ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, PR 178 ms, QTc 414 ms) was obtained before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025; QTc has increased by ~150 ms - see the QT_SAFETY item.

9/17/2024 tracing (only ECG on file): irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm, mean ventricular rate ~101 bpm (RR 0.41-1.07 s, RMSSD 256 ms), with no discernible or reproducible P waves - atrial fibrillation, so no measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms, QT 314 ms, QTc 408 ms, frontal axis about -48 degrees (lead I positive, II/III/aVF negative) = left axis deviation. Consistent with the atrial fibrillation coded 9/16/2024; he is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start - requirement met. (That ECG showed QTc ~563 ms, handled as a separate QT_SAFETY item.)

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 2025-08-22 (Condition 42731) and carried in the problem list of every subsequent cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025, 11/20/2025, 3/13/2026, 6/27/2026). No anticoagulant is or has been ordered; current medications are levothyroxine only (amiodarone was a brief peri-operative course ending 8/27/2025). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis = vascular disease 1), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. Note prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (2025-08-22) should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulant needs prescriber review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit (order valid to 1/4/2027) and is listed as a current medication, even though outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 document an upper GI bleed from a duodenal ulcer (admission 8/2-8/5/2026, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. Also on aspirin and clopidogrel. The decision to resume anticoagulation after a major bleed has not been documented and needs prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are current simultaneously. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026), and the note lists both drugs in the current medication list. Rivaroxaban was never stopped, so as of 9/24/2026 the patient has concurrent rivaroxaban and apixaban (plus clopidogrel) - a bleeding hazard requiring immediate reconciliation.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at about 142-144 bpm with no organised P waves (RR 0.35-0.72 s, RMSSD ~100 ms, no reproducible atrial deflection) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, and unspecified atrial fibrillation was coded for the same encounter. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the tracings; the note needs correction and rate/rhythm management reviewed.

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily (current clinic order 7/18/2026, valid to 12/26/2026; continuously prescribed since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~500 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~535 ms, which is >=500 ms and per the QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Potassium 3.8 mEq/L (3/18/2026) and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026) are normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven; note the 5/14/2024 clinic note called the QT 'acceptable' when starting escitalopram. A repeat ECG and review of QT-prolonging therapy are needed.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current clinic order 7/12/2026, valid to 1/9/2027; started at the 11/10/2025 clinic visit). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QT ~555 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~563 ms - markedly prolonged and >=500 ms, which requires prescriber review under the QT monitoring memo. QTc was 414 ms on the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025, so this is a drug-associated increase of ~150 ms. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Also on warfarin; amiodarone dose/continuation and repeat ECG need review.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily (current clinic order 7/15/2026, valid to 1/7/2027; on citalopram since 3/8/2025). Most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT ~505 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~549 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, requiring prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. QTc was 424 ms on the previous ECG (6/17/2020). Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised with QT prolongation; dose reduction and a repeat ECG should be considered.

95-year-old woman taking amiodarone 200 mg daily (current clinic order 6/17/2026, valid to 1/6/2027; on amiodarone since at least 2022). Most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a broad, late-peaking T wave: QT ~575 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~565 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold that requires prescriber review.
